scope: Sixth expansion batch: six before/after exercises, three per target. Paired contexts cover a past snack, a future departure plan and a recurring class expressed as a noun. Scope is the basic temporal mae/ato patterns, not spatial meanings, every reading of 前/後, or all temporal constructions in the article.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: BTS00130: structure diagram for dictionary-form verb or event noun + no before mae ni; explanation A for event order and C for dictionary form regardless of main-clause tense; past examples 3-6 and noun examples 7-9.

sources.publisher: The Japan Foundation, Minna no Kyozai
sources.section: BTS00129: structure diagram for Vta or event noun + no before ato de; explanation A for later order and C for ta regardless of main-clause tense; future/nonpast examples 1 and 5-6 and noun example 7.
Toki, section 2 and examples 3-4 and 8-9: event order and relative tense, with mae/ato paraphrases. Used to screen the overlapping temporal neighbor toki, not to claim unrestricted equivalence.
After I, examples 25 and 28-30: verbal and noun constructions with ato ni and subsequent actions. Independently inspected during review; cited for particle usage, not a universal immediacy rule.

authoringNotes: All exercise scenarios are newly authored. Sources support the constructions and timing principles; the scenarios and accepted answers still require independent editorial review.

Every English question explicitly requests mae or ato. Verb items additionally request the dictionary or ta form of the supplied verb; noun items print no. Ni is printed after every blank and must not be repeated in an answer.
Accepted spellings include kana and kanji for both the verb and mae/ato. Options and typed strings contain exactly the missing span, not a replacement for the whole sentence.

The source's ato de pattern supports event order and verb attachment. The exercises use ato ni for the stated temporal relation; feedback acknowledges ato de as another formulation rather than attaching de before the printed ni.

The past before-item and future after-item guard against selecting a subordinate verb form merely from yesterday or tomorrow. The timings refer to the same event instances, with explicit start or completion boundaries.
Both targets occur in all three paired frames, with one SRS identity per exercise. Do not count choose/type variants or relationship directions as additional exercises.

Screen the full article inventory while respecting the visible controlled task. Toki can also express before/after relations with suitable predicates; it is not excluded on a false rule that it must always be simultaneous.
The original 62 exercise records remain unchanged. Other temporal constructions and spatial mae/ato meanings are outside this batch.
